findings.title: Missing auth_token_threshold table causes safe_logout to panic at runtime
findings.suggested_fix: Create migration 017_create_token_threshold.sql: CREATE TABLE auth_token_threshold (person_unique VARCHAR(255) PRIMARY KEY, threshold_time TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP). Also update session.rs lines 137 and 292 which query the same table. Without this table, every call to safe_logout will fail with 'relation auth_token_threshold does not exist'.

findings.title: Missing change_password_time/password_expired_time columns crash login, two_factor, and switch_user handlers
findings.suggested_fix: Add ALTER TABLE to a new migration (017 or combined): ALTER TABLE auth_person ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS change_password_time TIMESTAMP, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS password_expired_time TIMESTAMP. Affected handlers: lib.rs:101 (login SELECT), lib.rs:120-121, two_factor.rs:53/63, switch_user.rs:42/59-60. Without these columns, every login/two_factor/switch_user call returns 500 Internal Server Error.

findings.title: Missing auth_identity and auth_person_identity tables crash identity-related queries
findings.suggested_fix: Create migration with: CREATE TABLE auth_identity (id VARCHAR(255) PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, deleted_at TIMESTAMP, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP); CREATE TABLE auth_person_identity (person_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, identity_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, PRIMARY KEY (person_id, identity_id), CONSTRAINT fk_pi_person FOREIGN KEY (person_id) REFERENCES auth_person(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, CONSTRAINT fk_pi_identity FOREIGN KEY (identity_id) REFERENCES auth_identity(id) ON DELETE CASCADE). Affected: lib.rs:181-188 (identity_list in login), batch_query.rs:172-209 (express_person_list identity branch), batch_query.rs:453 (express_person_with_identity). All calls to these endpoints will fail with 'relation auth_identity does not exist'.

findings.title: manager_list_paging SQL LIMIT/OFFSET parameters are in wrong order
findings.suggested_fix: Line 477: change &[&size, &offset] to &[&offset, &size]. The SQL uses LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2 but the parameters pass size first then offset. With page=1, size=10: currently sends LIMIT 10 OFFSET 10 (skips first 10, shows 10-20), should be LIMIT 10 OFFSET 0 (shows first 10). Also page=0 gives offset=0 (returns first page instead of error), which is acceptable but worth noting.

findings.title: Icon GET endpoint has permission registry mismatch: R8 requires public access but registry marks as Authenticated
findings.suggested_fix: Line 189: change `registry.register_prefix("/jaxrs/person/icon", PermissionLevel::Authenticated);` to `registry.register_prefix("/jaxrs/person/icon", PermissionLevel::Public);`. R8 explicitly states GET icon is accessible without authentication (无权限也可访问). The icon::get handler itself does no auth check, but the middleware will reject unauthenticated requests before reaching the handler.

findings.title: two_factor.rs bypasses LDAP authentication
findings.suggested_fix: Add LDAP check before password::verify_password, mirroring the pattern in lib.rs:130-141. After fetching the row, call ldap_auth::try_ldap_authenticate(&req.credential, &req.password).await and only fall through to password::verify_password if LDAP returns None (disabled) or false (failed, fallback). Without this, users who authenticate via LDAP cannot use the two-factor flow.

findings.title: remove_sessions_by_person deletes DB rows but in-memory removal has redundant double lock
findings.suggested_fix: Lines 237-248: The second write lock loop (line 246-248) is redundant because sessions were already removed in lines 237-244 under the first write lock. The collect-then-remove pattern creates two separate write lock acquisitions. Simplify to a single write lock pass that both collects and removes in one operation. This is low-severity because the end result is correct, but the double-lock is unnecessary contention.

findings.title: broadcast_logout has TOCTOU gap between read-lock enumeration and write-lock removal
findings.suggested_fix: Lines 308-319: The function acquires a read lock to enumerate expired sessions, releases it, then acquires a write lock to remove them. Between these two operations, a new session could be created for the same user that falls before the threshold but wasn't in the original enumeration. Fix by holding the write lock for both enumeration and removal in a single critical section, or accept the small race window as benign (the session will be cleaned up on next validate_session call via check_token_threshold).

findings.title: express_person_with_identity double-fetches person fields from joined row
findings.suggested_fix: Lines 466-469: When rows is not empty, the code does `rows[0].get("unique_id")` and `rows[0].get("name")` — but the SQL on line 453 already selects p.unique_id and p.name. However, when rows is empty, it falls back to `id.clone()` for unique and null for name, which is inconsistent (the id passed in may not match any person). This is a minor logic issue — consider using the input id directly and only filling name/unique from rows when available, or returning an empty identities array with the input id.

findings.title: empower manager endpoints lack ownership check (admin can modify anyone's empowerment)
findings.suggested_fix: Lines 394-416 (manager_update) and 424-445 (manager_delete): Admin bypass of require_owner means any admin can modify/delete any empowerment record. Per R28, admin can manage others' authorizations, but manager_update and manager_delete should arguably verify the admin has legitimate reason (e.g., the target to_person belongs to their org). This is a design-level concern; the current implementation follows the plan's 'admin bypass' pattern but may allow privilege escalation through empowerment content manipulation.

residual_risks: auth_token_threshold migration missing — if not created before deployment, safe_logout and all TokenThreshold checks will fail at runtime
change_password_time/password_expired_time columns missing — login, two_factor, and switch_user all query these; runtime 500 errors until migration is applied
auth_identity/auth_person_identity tables missing — identity_list queries in login response and batch query endpoints will fail with SQL errors
LDAP fallback is silent — no monitoring/alerting when LDAP auth fails and falls back to DB (plan-identified open question)
Batch query rate limiting uses shared rate limiter but has no per-endpoint cap beyond the 100-ID limit — sustained high-volume enumeration still possible

SessionManager broadcast_logout uses eventual consistency (read-then-write gap) — in high-concurrency multi-instance deployments, a session created milliseconds after enumeration may briefly survive logout
testing_gaps: No migration test verifies auth_token_threshold, change_password_time, password_expired_time, auth_identity, auth_person_identity tables exist before integration tests run
two_factor.rs has no LDAP integration test — the handler bypasses LDAP without any test coverage for the LDAP-enabled path
manager_list_paging LIMIT/OFFSET swap is not caught by any test — a correct test would verify page=2 returns different results than page=1
icon::get public access is not tested — permission registry currently blocks unauthenticated requests, so the endpoint would need a test with no token to verify the fix
batch_query.rs express_person_with_identity has no test for empty-result case (person has no identities)
safe_logout TokenThreshold write is not testable without the migration existing
